title: C-01: leaderboard parser stored the active streak in all_season/all_time snapshot rows (daily snapshots 5/01–7/04)
missing_evidence: a primary read of the stored rows: data/leaderboard/leaderboard_snapshots/<date>.parquet for any 2026-05-01..2026-07-04 date, all_season/all_time `streak` vs season_stats `best_streak` (C-01 reports the 2026-07-04 comparison; the file is not in the repo) — Phase 2 Route R; leaderboard snapshots are not among the §5 projections, so this needs an X-20 amendment or a count-only comparison
tier_reason: research-integrity failure if confirmed: for two months two of the four daily leaderboard tabs silently stored the active streak instead of the tab's ranking quantity and the files are not rewritten; the per-date all_time value was discarded and is stored nowhere, while the all_season value survives only through same-date season_stats profiles; no delivery/entry/state impact and no residual reaches production (B is arguable — see notes)

contract.text: Each leaderboard snapshot row's `streak` carries the tab's own ranking quantity from the MLB rank row: season best on all_season, all-time best on all_time, active streak on active_streak / yesterday.
contract.source: docs/audit/2026-09-corrections-index.md C-01; src/bts/leaderboard/scraper.py _tab_streak_fields docstring and the LeaderboardRow field comment (44df03f)

mechanism.text: parse_leaderboard_response set `streak` from `activeStreak` whenever present, for every tab, and stored no other streak field, so all_season and all_time rows recorded the active streak and dropped the tab's own `streak` (season / all-time best); run() wrote only the parsed rows to leaderboard_snapshots/<date>.parquet

mitigated.action: C-01 reading rule: pre-fix files are not rewritten; readers ignore `streak` on all_season/all_time in them and use season_stats best_streak or the 9/28 full-depth walk

residual.text: Daily snapshots 2026-05-01..07-04 keep the wrong `streak` for all_season/all_time (files not rewritten; no season_best_streak/active_streak columns); the season best of listed users is recoverable from same-date season_stats where the profile fetch succeeded, the per-date all-time best is not stored anywhere
residual.source: docs/audit/2026-09-corrections-index.md C-01; 44df03f body; src/bts/leaderboard/scraper.py run() and models.SeasonStats at 2b752be

watchdog.trigger: at each leaderboard snapshot write, an all_season or all_time tab whose stored ranking quantity is not non-increasing in rank, or whose stored value differs from the same response's raw `streak` field
watchdog.recovery_assertion: captures after the fix pass the invariant (the 44df03f test asserts a non-increasing season best by rank) and every pre-fix file is covered by the C-01 reading rule

evidence.locator: docs/audit/2026-09-corrections-index.md C-01 'What is wrong' (artifacts: data/leaderboard/leaderboard_snapshots/*.parquet on the box — not read)
evidence.what: C-01 (found 2026-09-22 in the Codex review of the final-grab wrapper, confirmed on box data) reports that the 2026-07-04 snapshot's all_season `streak` column disagrees with the profile-derived best_streak for most rows, and that every daily snapshot 2026-05-01 → 2026-07-04 is affected

evidence.locator: commit 44df03f message body and diff (src/bts/leaderboard/scraper.py, models.py, storage.py; docs/audit/2026-09-corrections-index.md C-01 row added)
evidence.what: the parser preferred activeStreak over streak for every tab; fixed to tab-specific semantics with new season_best_streak / active_streak columns and envelope validation; historical parquet files are not rewritten and C-01 records the reading rule

evidence.locator: src/bts/leaderboard/scraper.py at e6931e1 (2026-05-01) and 2b752be (parse_leaderboard_response, run); deploy/systemd/bts-leaderboard.timer at 07a0f60
evidence.what: the activeStreak-first assignment exists from the scraper's first commit; run() writes only parsed rows (no raw bodies); the timer scheduled the scrape twice daily (05:00 and 14:00 UTC)
2b752be (carries the activeStreak-first parser, lacks 44df03f) deployed 2026-06-07T00:11:21Z, canary passed: the defective parser was installed inside the 5/01–7/04 window
pre-deploy f1b07e9 -> deployed d15d382 at 2026-09-22T15:53:56Z, canary passed: the fix was first installed

evidence.locator: commit 49a8446 message body and ARCHITECTURE.md diff (written 2026-07-04T14:51:02-04:00)
evidence.what: bts-leaderboard.timer (the authenticated deep scrape) was disabled on the box on 7/04 after running twice daily at 01:00/10:00 ET, which ends the daily snapshot series

notes: disposition: the firing is established only by the 9/22 box-data confirmation (C-01 and the 44df03f body, written 4+ months later; artifact not read), which is reported evidence; code + deploy evidence (ev3, ev4) alone would support deployed_latent_defect if Route R cannot read the stored rows

ev6 is typed inference: written 7/04 about the timer, not about this defect, and the validator anchors the 48 h rule on the 5/01 onset

code cite 2b752be (log) is an ancestor of the fix parent 332414f with the identical parser line, installed per a retained log inside the window; 332414f itself was never installed during the window (candidate)
split?: 44df03f also added envelope validation (an error-only body parsed as an empty board) — a separate latent defect with no evidenced firing
no repo consumer read the wrong columns before the fix (bts.leaderboard.analysis.percentile_rank reads the active_streak tab only); C-01 requires any W2 memo on season-best distributions to cite it

tier A vs B: A because a research corpus was silently corrupted and the per-date all_time values are lost; B is arguable because C-01 caught it before any read and run() also profiled every listed user into season_stats (best_streak = seasonBestStreak), so season bests are recoverable
